tweets.text:
Here is an empirical validation of the two most interesting K3 claims:

1 - That it's less "intelligence-dense" thus expensive on a per task basis even if cheap on a per token basis
2 - That it's SOTA at creative writing and critical thinking

This eval set validated the "wastrel" (token-inefficient) nature of K3 that @GavinSBaker noted and, to my eye, that it's excellent at critical thinking / working with prose.

The background: I've been working on a project that unbundles my X bookmarks into opinions/claims and then connects ideas across posts, so I used it as a testbed: 10 frontier models each judged the same 40 claims against a ~3,000-claim knowledge base, examining per-task cost (one claim judged end-to-end) and quality of critical thinking (how credible + complete the connections were).

Anyways you can see the evals for yourself at the link below.
